pages.title: How to Extract DMC3 PAC Files — DMC Rengine
pages.description: DMC3 PAC extraction guide covering slot-preserving parsing, nested resources and evidence-bounded reintegration.
pages.summary: Extract DMC3 PAC resources without flattening away the slot structure that gives each payload its physical identity. DMC Rengine preserves sparse and empty entries, nested resource relationships and provenance so PAC extraction remains useful for later typed inspection and guarded authoring workflows.

sections.heading: PAC extraction follows slots, not just filenames
items: The canonical PAC path preserves physical slot identity, sparse and empty entries and nested payload relationships instead of presenting the container as a normal directory with anonymous extracted files.
A PAC child can itself be another container or a typed resource, so extraction continues through the resource graph until the useful leaf payload is reached and routed to the appropriate reader.
Size-changing relative-slot reflow exists for the supported authoring path, but that narrower capability is kept distinct from unrestricted edited-resource acceptance by the original runtime.

sections.heading: From PAC to the rest of the ecosystem
items: Materialized PAC children can be handed to DMC Rengine Native Reader integration modules such as MOD, SCM, DDS, PTX, HITS, SHW, DCA, LIG2 or Stage TXT when their format identity is established; this broader C++ registry must not be confused with the narrower Android app module set.

The current DMC Native Reader Android application promotes MOD, SCM, DDS and PTX, while GDSpaces keeps the parent container and slot provenance attached so downstream inspection can trace where each resource came from.

Use PAC extraction as one layer in the DMC3 unpacking funnel, then continue to model, texture or format-specific inspection according to the actual child resource and the capability promoted by the consuming application.

pages.title: How to Browse DMC3 PNST Containers — DMC Rengine
pages.description: DMC3 PNST browsing guide for slot identity, nested resources and typed reader handoff.
pages.summary: Browse PNST containers as structured DMC3 resource graphs rather than flat folders. DMC Rengine preserves slot identity, aliases, empty entries and provenance, then routes materialized children to typed readers when a canonical parser exists.

sections.heading: PNST browsing preserves container meaning
items: PNST slots are kept as part of resource identity, including sparse, empty and alias relationships that would be lost if every payload were simply dumped into one normalized directory.
Recursive expansion lets a PNST child lead to another container or to a typed resource, with each transition recorded through the GDSpaces provenance-oriented resource graph.
The browsing layer therefore answers both what bytes were found and where those bytes originated inside the physical container hierarchy.

sections.heading: Typed inspection after PNST
items: When a leaf resource belongs to a canonical DMC Rengine reader family, the user can move from raw container browsing into structured model, scene, texture, collision, configuration or executable inspection according to the consuming tool's promoted capabilities.

Recognition and inspection remain weaker claims than editing or writer authority, so opening a PNST child does not automatically advertise modification or original-game reintegration support for that child format.

GDSpaces/PocketGDS provide archive and resource navigation; the current DMC Native Reader Android app provides promoted MOD, SCM, DDS and PTX leaf inspection; DMC Rengine remains the broader C++20 parser, integration and evidence authority.

pages.title: How to Find Dante Models and Textures in DMC3 HD — DMC Rengine
pages.description: Find Dante-related DMC3 model and texture resources through provenance-aware archive, MOD and DDS/PTX inspection.
pages.summary: A character-focused entry point for users searching for Dante models or textures rather than binary format names. The workflow starts from the DMC3 resource hierarchy, verifies candidate MOD resources with the canonical model reader and follows texture relationships into PTX or DDS-bearing resources without relying on one guessed universal filename.

sections.heading: Search by character, verify by resource structure
items: Start with the archive and container hierarchy, preserve the member and slot provenance and then verify candidate model data through the canonical MOD reader instead of treating a plausible filename as sufficient evidence.

The current MOD reader exposes hierarchy, transforms, meshes, texture-slot state and skinning-related data strongly enough to distinguish a real structured model resource from an arbitrary binary payload.

For texture work, follow model-facing relationships into the texture layer and distinguish PTX bundles, descriptor-plus-DDS slots and directly recognizable DDS resources rather than collapsing them into one texture identity.

sections.heading: Why there is no hard-coded universal Dante path
items: DMC Rengine treats archive member identity, slot provenance and build-specific evidence as first-class data, so one static filename or slot number is not promoted as universal without corpus proof across the intended scope.
This approach is more useful for future tooling because the same guide remains valid when the resource graph discovers the relevant character assets through another archive or container path.
The page therefore serves the common Dante model and texture search intent while still routing users into canonical MOD and DDS/PTX research for technical authority.

pages.title: How to Extract DMC3 Stage Models and Scene Resources — DMC Rengine
pages.description: DMC3 stage extraction guide connecting NBZ/PAC/PNST materialization to SCM, MOD and related stage resources.
pages.summary: Extract DMC3 stage-related resources while keeping scene geometry, models, collision and configuration families distinct. The workflow preserves NBZ and container provenance, then routes SCM, MOD, HITS, Stage TXT, LIG/LIG2 and other children to their proper canonical readers instead of labeling every stage payload as one model format.

sections.heading: Stage extraction is a resource-family problem
items: The outer archive path can lead through PAC or PNST before reaching a stage-related child, so preserving the physical resource path is necessary before any geometry or configuration semantics are assigned.
SCM is the primary scene-oriented geometry research surface, while MOD remains a separate model family and HITS, Stage TXT, LIG/LIG2 or DCA each carry their own structural responsibilities.
Classifying the leaf resource before inspection prevents a viewer from forcing collision, configuration and scene data into one misleading generic stage-model representation.

sections.heading: Inspect first, author only under proven contracts
items: The SCM reader supports scene-node, object, mesh, stream and transform analysis, which is enough for strong read-side stage inspection without claiming universal scene editing.
Texture references should be followed into the separate texture resource layer rather than treated as embedded image identity, preserving the same evidence discipline used for character models.
Any stage rebuild or original-game acceptance claim remains tied to the relevant writer and runtime proof gates instead of inheriting authority merely because extraction and structural reading work.

pages.title: How to Inspect DMC3 Animations and MOT Research — DMC Rengine
pages.description: DMC3 animation inspection guide connecting MOD hierarchy and pose data to the evidence-gated MOT research frontier.
pages.summary: Inspect DMC3 animation relationships without pretending MOD owns every motion semantic. MOT is present in the broader DMC Rengine C++ Native Reader integration registry, while the current DMC Native Reader Android app does not promote MOT in its main module set. Animation authoring and original-runtime acceptance remain separate proof gates.

sections.heading: Begin from the promoted model node domain
items: The canonical MOD path already exposes hierarchy, local and world transforms, motion-group values and skin-palette relationships strongly enough to provide the model-side context required for pose-aware animation research.

Animation data should be related to that node domain instead of assigning bone or motion meaning from filenames alone, because hierarchy nodes and higher-level animation semantics are not automatically identical concepts.
The resulting workflow can support debugging of animation binding and evaluated poses while keeping the source evidence and unresolved ownership boundaries visible.

sections.heading: MOT registry presence and Android app promotion are different claims
items: The canonical DMC Rengine Native Reader integration registry includes a MOT module, so C++ integration presence is real and should not be described as absent.

The current DMC Native Reader Android application main remains intentionally narrower and promotes MOD, SCM, DDS and PTX rather than MOT, so this page does not advertise completed Android MOT viewing.

Complete animation authoring, universal MOT revision coverage and edited-motion original-game acceptance require their own proof gates and are not implied by registry presence or pose-aware MOD inspection.
